speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying the timing and nature of your pain. When did the shooting ear pain begin relative to your tympanoplasty, and does it worsen when you touch the outer ear or try to insert an earring?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain when eating suggests possible involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve; are these shooting pains accompanied by facial twitching or drooping? Additionally, does the discomfort when wearing earrings feel like deep aching or sharp stabbing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (tic douloureux) secondary to post-tympanoplasty scarring or nerve entrapment. The pain triggered by chewing and the specific distribution suggest this rather than a simple surgical complication or infection.
